title: API 510 Training in Chicago: Pressure Vessel Exam Prep
description: API 510 exam prep for Chicago-area vessel inspectors: Whiting, Joliet and Morris equipment, Illinois and Indiana rules, self-paced online with instructor Q&A.
h1: API 510 training in Chicago: exam preparation for inspectors of refinery, olefins and chemical plant pressure vessels
html:
API 510 exam prep for Chicagoland pressure vessel inspectors

Chicago's pressure vessel work does not happen downtown. It happens on the Lake Michigan shore in north-west Indiana, beside the Des Plaines River in Will County, at a refinery in Lemont and in the chemical and polymer plants that follow the Illinois River towards Morris. Fractionators, coke drums, reactors, separators and a great many shell-and-tube exchangers sit in those plants, and each needs somebody who can read its thickness history, work out what it can still safely hold and decide when it must be opened again. That is the job the API 510 Pressure Vessel Inspector certification describes.

Atlantis NDT's course is exam preparation for it: self-paced and online, with an instructor who answers your questions as you work. There is no Atlantis classroom in Chicago, and none is needed, because everything runs on the learning portal; Atlantis's offices are in Houston and Hyderabad. The American Petroleum Institute sets the eligibility rules, administers the examination at Prometric test centres and issues the certification to candidates who pass.

Where the pressure vessels are: Whiting, Joliet, Lemont and the Morris corridor

The U.S. Energy Information Administration's refinery capacity report, which lists every operable refinery as of January 2026, shows three large refineries within a commute of the Loop. Each has the distillation, coking and conversion units that put hundreds of vessels under an owner-user inspection programme, and an olefins and polyethylene complex further down the river adds a different kind of vessel population.

SitePublished figuresVessel work an API 510 inspector meets there
bp's Whiting refinery, Whiting, Indiana435,000 barrels per calendar day of crude distillation in EIA's 2026 listing (bp states about 440,000 a day), with 102,000 barrels per stream day of delayed coking and 177,000 of catalytic crackingCrude and vacuum columns, coke drums, the FCC reactor and regenerator, hydrotreater reactors and separators, sulfur recovery vessels
ExxonMobil's Joliet refinery, Channahon Township, Will County275,000 barrels a day of crude capacity on about 1,400 acres, started up by Mobil in 1972; EIA lists 58,500 barrels per stream day of delayed coking and 100,300 of catalytic crackingTwelve major process units, a cogeneration facility, LPG storage and the drums and exchangers between them
A refinery at Lemont, Illinois188,023 barrels per calendar day of crude distillation in EIA's 2026 listing, with delayed coking and catalytic crackingA coking refinery's columns, drums, reactors and exchanger banks
LyondellBasell's Morris plant, Grundy CountyProduces ethylene, propylene and low-density, linear low-density and high-density polyethyleneFractionators, compressor knock-out drums, polymer reactors and the cold-section equipment of an olefins plant

Smaller sites add to the count, among them the plant Stepan lists at Millsdale, near Joliet. Most full-time API 510 work, though, sits with refinery and petrochemical owner-user inspection groups and the contractors that staff their turnarounds. bp says Whiting averages about 1,500 contractors on site, and ExxonMobil lists roughly 580 employees plus contractors at Joliet.

What heavy crude means for a vessel inspector in this region

Whiting's 2013 modernization changed the local vessel picture more than any other recent project. Oil & Gas Journal reported that it brought on a 102,000 barrel-a-day coker, a reconfigured 250,000 barrel-a-day crude unit (the largest of the refinery's three) and a 105,000 barrel-a-day gas oil hydrotreater, and that heavy, sour crude, Canadian bitumen among it, could afterwards make up more than 80% of the feed, against about 20% before. ExxonMobil says Joliet runs Canadian crude delivered by pipeline as well. That kind of crude pushes a recognisable set of damage mechanisms up a local vessel inspector's list, and most are in the API RP 571 selection the current API 510 Body of Knowledge examines:

  • Sulfidation and naphthenic acid corrosion (RP 571 paragraphs 3.61 and 3.46) in the hot sections of crude, vacuum and coker units. Know which alloys resist each and how the attack looks.
  • High-temperature hydrogen attack and high-temperature H2/H2S corrosion (3.36 and 3.35) in hydrotreater reactor circuits.
  • Hydrochloric acid corrosion (3.37) in crude tower overhead drums and condensers, where chlorides that get past the desalter turn into acid as the vapour condenses.
  • Wet H2S damage and amine stress corrosion cracking (3.67 and 3.3) in sour water strippers, amine contactors and regenerators.
  • Brittle fracture (3.11), which a Chicago winter makes very real: cold start-ups and January hydrotests on thick vessels bring the minimum design metal temperature into play.

Two things a local candidate meets at work are not on the examined list. Coke drums suffer thermal fatigue, bulging and cracking from their fill-and-quench cycle, but the current Body of Knowledge contains no thermal fatigue paragraph, so drum fatigue is a job skill rather than an examined topic. And the BOK excludes cryogenic vessels below −50°F, which takes the coldest olefins plant equipment out of the examination. Check the BOK for your own window, because API revises the list.

Three inspection authorities around one city

A Chicagoland vessel inspector can cross two jurisdictional lines in a working week. The API certificate replaces none of the rules on either side; it shows you know the in-service code most refinery vessel programmes are built on.

Inside the City of Chicago

The Boiler Inspection Bureau of the city's Department of Buildings makes external inspections of boilers and unfired pressure vessels while they operate, internal inspections of pressure vessels when necessary, first inspections after installation permits and hydrostatic tests after installation or extensive repair. Repairs must be made by a boiler repairer the City licenses.

The rest of Illinois

Outside the city, the Office of the State Fire Marshal's Division of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety administers the state act. Under Subpart F of 41 Ill. Adm. Code 2120, the State Fire Marshal authorises as owner-users only firms that meet Section 15 of the act and keep a written quality control system acceptable to the Chief Inspector; the Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Rules decides each application, and the Division audits accepted programmes every year. For a Joliet or Lemont candidate, that quality control manual ties the plant's API 510 work to state law.

North-west Indiana

Whiting, Hammond and East Chicago fall under the Boilers and Pressure Vessels Section of Indiana's Department of Homeland Security, which enforces 675 IAC 30. A regulated vessel may not operate without a state operating permit, permit inspections must be made by an Indiana-licensed inspector, and pressure vessel permits run for one, two or three years depending on the vessel. The licence comes from a National Board commission or equivalent, a reciprocal state licence or the Department's own examination, so a Whiting inspector may need it as well as API 510.

Worked example: static head at the bottom of a tall column

Columns are where Chicago candidates often lose static head marks, because the governing shell course sits at the bottom, under the liquid, not at the nameplate pressure at the top. Take a debutanizer-type column designed for 150 psig at the top. The bottom course has 25 ft of liquid with a specific gravity of 0.8 above it, the inside radius is 72 in., the problem gives an allowable stress of 20,000 psi and the longitudinal joint efficiency is 0.85.

  1. Static head at the bottom course: 25 × 0.433 × 0.8 = 8.66 psi, so the course is designed for 158.66 psi.
  2. Required thickness under UG-27(c)(1): t = PR ÷ (SE − 0.6P) = (158.66 × 72) ÷ (17,000 − 95.2) = 11,423.5 ÷ 16,904.8 = 0.676 in.
  3. Readings at the governing CML: 0.940 in. sixteen years ago, 0.870 in. eight years ago, 0.820 in. today. Long-term rate = 0.120 ÷ 16 = 0.0075 in. per year; short-term = 0.050 ÷ 8 = 0.00625. With nothing to say otherwise, use the higher figure.
  4. Remaining corrosion allowance = 0.820 − 0.676 = 0.144 in.; remaining life = 0.144 ÷ 0.0075 = 19.2 years.
  5. Internal or on-stream interval = the lesser of half the remaining life and 10 years: 9.6 years.

Now the trap. Leave out the static head and the required thickness drops to 0.639 in., the remaining life rises to 24.2 years and the interval is capped at 10 years. The answers look close, which is exactly why the wrong one appears among the options; on a column holding deeper or denser liquid the gap widens, and in the field the same mistake points the inspection plan at the wrong course.

Who sits API 510 around Chicago, and the route each takes

API looks at education plus pressure vessel experience gained in the last ten years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency, which includes an owner-user inspection organisation. The API 510 certification requirements page has the detail; locally, candidates arrive by four routes.

  • NDT technicians. Field service companies in the suburbs hire Level I and Level II technicians for refinery and outage work, and Moraine Valley Community College in the south-west suburbs has run noncredit NDT classes in penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic and radiation safety. With a high school diploma, API asks for three years of vessel experience, one of them performing or supervising inspection. Atlantis's NDT training for Chicago covers the SNT-TC-1A route into that work.
  • Boilermakers and welders. Years fabricating and repairing vessels count towards the total, but the inspection year has to be earned in an inspection role; welding inspection is a common step between, described on the AWS CWI exam prep for Chicago page.
  • Operators. Operating experience counts too, and many local inspectors moved from a unit's operating crew into the plant inspection department, where they built their inspection year.
  • Engineers. A bachelor's degree in engineering or technology needs one year supervising or performing inspection. Purdue University Northwest teaches its mechanical engineering degree on both its Hammond and Westville campuses, so a local graduate in an inspection or reliability group can qualify quickly.

Technical military service counts as education, three or more years like a bachelor's degree, unless the discharge was dishonorable. API verifies the experience you document, so keep a record of vessels and tasks as you go.

Studying for API 510 around Chicago turnarounds and winters

The local calendar shapes preparation more than any study technique. Refinery turnarounds bring weeks of twelve-hour shifts, and nobody studies Section VIII well in the middle of one. The portal keeps your place, so you stop for the turnaround and resume afterwards without falling behind anyone. Many use the darker months for the heaviest reading and aim at a window after their own site's busiest weeks. Collect questions from the job as you go: a radiography marking on a nameplate you cannot interpret, a corrosion rate the plant software calculated differently from your hand figure, or a repair the shift supervisor called an alteration. The instructor answers from the code text, so you learn where the answer sits as well as what it is.

Sitting the API 510 exam from Chicago

API 510 is taken in person, and Prometric lists test centres in and around Chicago. Book once API has accepted your application, and allow for the drive: a candidate from Whiting or Channahon may cross the metro at rush hour. The day is 7.5 hours, with 110 closed-book questions in 2.75 hours, a 45-minute lunch and 60 open-book questions in 3.75 hours; 140 of the 170 questions are scored. In the open-book half the examined documents are PDFs on screen, and your tabbed copies stay at home. API runs the exam in set windows, each with its own application deadline, listed on the API exam schedule page; the API 510 code explainer is a useful companion for the code itself.

Ways to prepare in Chicago, compared

  • Intensive seminars. Several training companies run concentrated API 510 seminars before exam windows, in person or online at fixed times. They suit someone who already knows the codes and can be released for the dates.
  • Employer programmes. Large owner-user groups mentor their own people, which teaches the plant's procedures and software as no outside course can, though not always the Body of Knowledge or open-book technique.
  • Self-paced online study with instructor Q&A. The Atlantis format suits rotating shifts, contract work that moves between Whiting, Joliet and the Gulf Coast, and candidates who need to repeat the calculations before they stick.

With any provider, ask whether the material follows the editions on your window's Publications Effectivity Sheet and whether it includes timed papers that copy the real split. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider, and the certificate comes only from passing API's examination.

Sponsoring API 510 candidates from a Chicago-area site

Owner-users and inspection contractors here often prepare several people at once, for example before a contract that names API 510 inspectors or as experienced unit inspectors near retirement. One enquiry can cover the group, and fees are quoted on request. Eligibility stays personal, so check each person's experience record before enrolling them. In the United States Atlantis performs UT, MT, PT and VT inspection and does not perform radiography; its ultrasonic testing services for Chicago describe the field side.

faq.q: Can I attend an API 510 class in person in Chicago?
faq.a: Not with Atlantis. There is no Atlantis classroom in the Chicago area; the API 510 course is studied online at your own pace, with an instructor answering your questions, and you start when you enrol. Other providers run seminars on fixed dates. Whichever preparation you use, the examination itself is sat in person at a Prometric test centre after API has accepted your application.

faq.q: Does the City of Chicago Boiler Inspection Bureau require API 510 certification?
faq.a: The bureau's page describes city inspections of boilers and unfired pressure vessels and requires repairs by a boiler repairer the City licenses; it says nothing about API 510. API 510 is a private certification that owner-user programmes and contracts ask for. Inside city limits the bureau's inspectors still carry out the inspections the Municipal Code requires, whatever certificates the plant's own inspectors hold.

faq.q: Do coke drums at Whiting count toward API 510 experience, and are they examined?
faq.a: Inspection work on coke drums is pressure vessel inspection, so it can count towards the experience API requires, provided it was done while employed by or under contract to an authorized inspection agency. The exam is another matter: the current Body of Knowledge lists no thermal fatigue paragraph from RP 571, so drum cycling damage is not an examined topic, while sulfidation and naphthenic acid corrosion are.

faq.q: I work at the Morris olefins plant. Are cold-section vessels on the API 510 exam?
faq.a: Only partly. The current Body of Knowledge excludes cryogenic vessels below −50°F, so the coldest equipment in an ethylene plant is outside the examination. Impact testing, minimum design metal temperature and the UCS-66 exemption rules are examined, and so is brittle fracture from RP 571. Your work on knock-out drums, fractionators and polymer reactors still counts as pressure vessel experience.

faq.q: Does an Indiana boiler and pressure vessel inspector licence replace API 510?
faq.a: No. Indiana's licence lets you make the permit inspections the state requires under 675 IAC 30, and it is earned through a National Board commission or equivalent, a reciprocal state licence or the Department's examination. API 510 is a separate certification that refinery owner-users ask for in their own programmes. Many inspectors at Whiting-area sites end up holding both.

faq.q: I graduated in mechanical engineering from Purdue Northwest. How soon can I sit API 510?
faq.a: With a bachelor's degree in engineering, API asks for one year of supervising or performing pressure vessel inspection, gained while employed by or under contract to an authorized inspection agency. Join a plant inspection or reliability group, or an inspection contractor, keep a record of the vessels you inspect, and apply once you have the year. You can begin the self-paced course before then.

faq.q: Can a Joliet or Hammond contractor enrol several API 510 candidates together?
faq.a: Yes. Send one enquiry with the number of candidates and the exam windows they are aiming at, and the quote covers the group. Each person studies at their own pace with access to the instructor, then applies to API individually and sits the examination individually. Check each candidate's documented experience first, because API decides eligibility person by person.
